item.title: index
item.description: United Kingdom 1946–Present The years after 1945 opened a new chapter for the United Kingdom.

item.title: Michael Herman — Intelligence Power in Peace and War (1996)
item.description: Former GCHQ/Cabinet Office practitioner's RIIA–Cambridge treatise on intelligence as an instrument of state: collection and all-source assessment, national and international effects, failure, community management, and post–Cold War value, drawn from British and American examples.

item.title: Arnold Toynbee — Surviving the Future (1971)
item.description: Recast of Toynbee’s 1971 dialogue with Kei Wakaizumi (originally serialised in the Mainichi Shimbun): seven essays on life’s purpose, technology, religion, education, society under technological pressure, and the student generation as first citizens of one world.

item.title: Arnold Toynbee and Daisaku Ikeda — The Toynbee–Ikeda Dialogue: Man Himself Must Choose (1976)
item.description: Kodansha record of Toynbee’s London conversations with Soka Gakkai president Daisaku Ikeda, edited by Richard L. Gage: personal and social life, political and international life (United States, Japan and Britain, war, one world), and philosophical and religious life.

item.title: Onassis: An Extravagant Life
item.description: Frank Brady’s 1977 popular biography of Aristotle Onassis, from Smyrna childhood and the 1922 fire through Argentine tobacco, flag-of-convenience tankers, the U.S. surplus-ship indictment, the Saudi/ARAMCO contract, Monaco, Peruvian whaling, Churchill, Callas and Jacqueline Kennedy to his death in March 1975.

item.title: The City
item.description: Tony Norfield’s analysis of London as the world’s financial broker, arguing that British imperialism after 1945 rebuilt itself through dollar euromarkets, dealing revenues, and a privileged place in the Anglo-American system—not as Wall Street’s satellite but as a second pole extracting value from the global hierarchy.

item.title: The People's Peace
item.description: Kenneth O. Morgan’s narrative political history of Britain since 1945 (fourth and revised edition, OUP 2021), from Attlee and the post-war settlement through Thatcherism, New Labour, the financial crisis, and Brexit.

item.title: Britain Since 1945
item.description: Multi-author Making Contemporary Britain survey (Hollowell, ed., Blackwell 2003) covering post-war politics, society, and economy in twenty-three thematic chapters from foreign policy and the constitution through devolution, race, health, and the welfare state.

item.title: How the British Invented Communism
item.description: Richard Poe’s 2024 polemic arguing that British imperial strategy—not primarily German sponsorship or a Jewish conspiracy—drove the Russian Revolution, invented modern communism as a weapon against rivals and the middle class, and that Round Table globalism continues that project to the present.

item.title: Dope, Inc. (4th edition)
item.description: 2010 EIR / Progressive Press compilation updating the Dope, Inc. thesis: LaRouche’s war plan against drugs, British-centred narcotics finance, Afghan opium, Soros and decriminalisation, a ~$600 billion trade, and reprinted core chapters from earlier editions on Opium Wars and organized crime.
